title: Fixed Income and Credit Assessment
description: 12 questions across 2 sections. Allow 40 minutes. Calculations state their units and rounding; review links identify the relevant lessons. The practice pass mark is 80 percent, not an employer certification.

questions.prompt: A one-year zero pays 100 at maturity. At a 5% annual yield, what is its price in currency units? Round to 4 places.
questions.explanation: Price is 100/1.05=95.238095, rounded to 95.2381. Subtracting five from face value is not annual discounting.

questions.prompt: A two-year bond pays an annual coupon of 5 and principal 100 at maturity. At a 5% annual yield, what is price in currency units?
questions.explanation: Discount 5 at year one and 105 at year two: 5/1.05+105/1.05**2=100. Equal coupon rate and yield give par under these conventions.

questions.prompt: A three-year zero-coupon bond has annual yield 5%. What is modified duration in years? Round to 4 places.
questions.explanation: Macaulay duration of a zero is its maturity, three years. Modified duration is 3/(1.05)=2.857143, not the maturity itself.

questions.prompt: A position worth 2,000,000 has modified duration 4. What is approximate positive DV01 magnitude in currency units per basis point?
questions.explanation: DV01 magnitude is price times modified duration times 0.0001: 2,000,000*4*0.0001=800. A yield rise produces a price loss, but the question asks magnitude.

questions.prompt: What is the first-order price effect of a small yield increase on a conventional fixed-rate bond?
options: Price rises by exactly its coupon
Price falls, holding other inputs fixed
questions.explanation: Positive duration means a negative first derivative of price with respect to yield for conventional positive cash flows. Convexity modifies the approximation for larger changes.

questions.prompt: Which statement separates a spot rate from a par coupon rate?
options: Spot is the realised holding-period return on every coupon bond
Spot discounts one dated flow; par coupon prices a bond at par
Spot and par both equal all future forward rates at every date
Par coupon discounts only principal; spot ignores coupons entirely
questions.explanation: A spot curve discounts individual dated cash flows. A par coupon is the coupon rate that makes a multi-cash-flow bond price equal face value under that curve.

questions.prompt: Under constant annual hazard 0.02, what is five-year survival probability? Give a decimal to 6 places.
questions.explanation: Survival is exp(-lambda*T)=exp(-0.1)=0.904837. One minus this value is default probability, not survival.

questions.prompt: In the continuous-premium flat-hazard CDS model, hazard is 0.02 and recovery 40%. What is annual par spread in basis points?
questions.explanation: The simplified spread is (1-0.4)*0.02=0.012, which is 120 basis points. Real discrete contract conventions require a fuller valuation.

questions.prompt: Why is a market-implied hazard rate not automatically a physical default frequency?
options: It also reflects risk-neutral pricing and model assumptions
It is measured without any price or recovery input
It guarantees the issuer will default on a known date
It removes liquidity and recovery uncertainty exactly
questions.explanation: Calibration produces pricing parameters conditional on recovery, discounting and risk premia. Those parameters are not direct promises about real-world future default counts.

questions.prompt: Which factor can create a CDS-bond basis without a free arbitrage?
options: Identical executable cash flows with zero costs always
A universal law forcing every bond to trade at par
Different funding, liquidity or settlement terms
A guarantee that all reference obligations are identical
questions.explanation: Funding, liquidity, deliverability and settlement differences can leave residual costs and risks. Comparing only mid spreads ignores the actual trade and financing contract.

questions.prompt: Why can duration alone understate approximation error for a large yield move?
questions.modelAnswer: Duration is a first-order sensitivity; convexity captures curvature, and larger moves require higher-order or full repricing.
questions.explanation: The tangent approximation ignores curvature. A larger yield move makes that omission more material, so recompute cash-flow present values or include appropriate higher-order terms.

questions.prompt: Name the information needed before comparing two credit-spread quotes.
questions.modelAnswer: Match issuer and seniority, maturity, currency and spread measure, then inspect recovery, liquidity, funding and settlement assumptions.
questions.explanation: Different instruments can carry the same issuer name but different cash flows and risks. A basis comparison needs compatible conventions and executable financing terms.
